title: Designing a Workflow Repository knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Designing a Workflow Repository?
options: A workflow repository should make CI, security, deployment, custom actions, reusable workflows, and configuration ownership easy to discover and review.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: A workflow repository should make CI, security, deployment, custom actions, reusable workflows, and configuration ownership easy to discover and review.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of designing a workflow repository: A workflow repository should make CI, security, deployment, custom actions, reusable workflows, and configuration ownership easy to discover and review. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Separating CI, security, and deployment workflows”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
questions.explanation: Separating CI, security, and deployment workflows: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to designing a workflow repository?
options: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: A workflow repository should make CI, security, deployment, custom actions, reusable workflows, and configuration ownership easy to discover and review. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
